pages.text: "I want to hold the baby!" Soso the quiet hedgehog scurried to the stove. Grandma Bear's baby grandchild sat on her lap, moving its feet. Soso wanted to hold and rock the baby bear.
Soso quickly hugged the baby with both arms. "Ouch!" A spine from Soso's back poked the baby's cheek. The baby's face crumpled.
"Waaah!" The baby cried. Startled, Soso curled into a ball, making their spines even stiffer. In Grandma's arms, the baby wouldn't look at Soso.
By the stove, the baby rattled a wooden spoon. Farther away, Soso fiddled only with their orange ribbon. "Maybe I shouldn't hold the baby."
Grandma sat beside Soso and stroked their back gently with her palm. The spines settled, making the back soft. "See how soft when they lie down? Your tummy side is soft from the start."
Grandma tapped Soso's tummy. "For a hug, tummy side, gently!" Soso looked down. There wasn't a single spine. Soso repeated softly, "Tummy side, gently!"
With tummy forward, Soso sat still beside the baby. No grabbing, just arms open wide and waiting. The baby rested its forehead softly against Soso's tummy.
Soso slowly straightened from their curl. Their back spines lay flat too. The baby put a little hand on that back and patted it. No prickles now.

Logs crackled in the stove. Soso showed the baby two open arms. "One, turn tummy side forward! Two, spines down! Three, wait until the baby comes!" The baby toddled over and snuggled into Soso's arms.

Grandma lifted both onto her lap and turned them toward the stove. Even a pointy back feels wonderfully soft when spines lie down and the tummy is offered. Soso whispered to the baby, "It doesn't hurt now, right? Tummy side, gently!"
